note: Dio calls the emperor by his own name, Gaius. "Caligula", "little boot", was a nickname from the soldiers he grew up among, and is the name later writers use.

Dio calls Caracalla by his official name, Antoninus, and sometimes by a nickname, Tarautas. "Caracalla", from the long hooded cloak he wore and gave out, is the name later writers use. (Later in Book 79 "Antoninus" is Elagabalus, the "False Antoninus".)
Until his death and its aftermath (to 79.10), Dio's "Antoninus" is Caracalla, also called Tarautas. From 79.11 the book is Macrinus's reign, and its "Antoninus" is Elagabalus, the "False Antoninus".
